newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Demand said to be slow for South American soymeal.
newsitem.headline: Demand said to be slow for South American soymeal.

text.p: Argentine soybean crushers are heading for a buildup of unusually large meal stocks, due to slacker than expected demand from Far Eastern buyers, local traders said Monday.

"Meal demand is relatively pooor," a trader told Reuters, "The carry-over we are expecting in Argentina for bean oil on September 30 will be almost a record low while we expect almost double the old record for meal stocks."
He said he expected Argentina's September 30 meal carry over to total about a million tonnes of soybeans and pellets.
"Given the inverted meal market, the crush is obliged to go at full blast despite poor margins. In some cases they're not covering their variable costs," he said.

"We are definitely not crushing for meal, here we are crushing because the markets are inverted," he added, "I expect Argentina will be a more important supplier of meal than oil from October 1, and the same for Brazil."
But other traders disagreed, saying the carry-over was unlikely to be so large.
"That's way too much. I expect to see the carry-over we have every month, about 500,000-600,000 tonnes," one said.
He added that sales were running at about 300,000-400,000 tonnes a month.
"There was some buying from Northern Europe last week. With prices slipping, there was a bit of bottom fishing. But with this latest rise in Chicago, the demand has vanished."
Another trader said, "It seems from the shipping lineup that there have been good sales for for July, August, September, more than last month. A million tonnes carry over seems too much to me."
He said Argentine meal was offered at $40 under August CBOT for August loading.
While meal sales are sluggish, South American oil sales are keeping up a good clip, although European rape seed oil is beginning to appear to slow Mediterranean demand.
"Oil sales are coming along, with the usual buyers," a trader said, "The Chinese are definitely active. The Iranians have been active."
He added, "But European rape oil is at a discount to bean oils so that means that Mediterranean destinations are covered from Europe, so demand for South America oil is slowing down."
He said Argentina and Brazil were still shipping 500,000 tonnes a month of soybean and sunflower seed oil.
